name: Sensitivity
summary: How far the mouse travels for a full turn. XIM says to start here.

intro.text: Mouse sensitivity is set in cm/360: the distance, in centimetres, for a full turn. A lower number is a shorter distance, so a faster turn.

citations.quote: Mouse sensitivity is in cm/360 or "distance (in centimeters) to perform a full turn". That means, lower values produce faster aiming speeds.

start.text: XIM says to start with Sensitivity alone, and to change other values only if you need to. There is no right set of values; it is preference.

citations.quote: Always start with just adjusting Sensitivity. Change other values only if necessary. There is no "right" set of values. It is preference that matches your gaming style.

statement.text: Lower the cm/360 for a faster aiming speed.

citations.quote: That means, lower values produce faster aiming speeds.

statement.text: Raise the cm/360 for a slower aiming speed: a longer distance for the same turn.

citations.quote: Mouse sensitivity is in cm/360 or "distance (in centimeters) to perform a full turn". That means, lower values produce faster aiming speeds.

statement.reasoning: XIM states the effect of lower values. cm/360 is the distance for one full turn, so a higher value is a longer distance for the same turn: slower.

notes.text: Thumbstick aim is not set in cm/360. Depending on the Config it is set in the game, or as a percentage of the game's maximum turn speed.

citations.quote: Depending on the type of Config, thumbstick sensitivity may be set through your in-game aim ettings, or, specified as a percentage (%) of maximum turn speed split between X and Y.

notes.text: If a game requires Simulate Analog Behavior, XIM's checklist says not to go faster than 20 cm/360.

citations.quote: Make sure your mouse sensitivity isn't faster than 20 cm/360.
